title: Case study report
context: Results from the corrected replay, including subsequent work beyond the original six-hour exercise.

parts.title: Part 1 — Discovery and triage
answer: Ranked 50 datasets from 1,509 deduplicated CKAN records. Outputs retain IDs, titles, publishers, formats, scores and reasons. The 100-point rubric uses business evidence (45), valid identifiers (20), corporate-name patterns (10), business names (10), identifier–name agreement (10) and catalogue category (5); it is not a probability.

Agentic triage assesses actual file previews instead of relying on potentially ambiguous descriptions. Human review confirmed all 20 sampled resources: 0/20 false positives (0% in this sample). The demo shows up to 50 rows per audited resource.

parts.title: Part 2 — Schema inference and mapping
selection: Six sources provide complementary identity, purpose, financial, service and regulatory data across ZIP/TSV, XLSX, CSV and JSON. ASIC Credit and another ATO year extend coverage to eight extracts/seven families:

dataset_contributions.name: ASIC Companies
dataset_contributions.detail: Identifiers, current/former names, registration, legal form and status.

dataset_contributions.name: ACNC
dataset_contributions.detail: Charitable purpose, beneficiaries, size bands, websites, contact addresses and operating regions.

dataset_contributions.name: ATO, two years
dataset_contributions.detail: Total income, taxable income and tax payable, with reporting periods.

dataset_contributions.name: DEWR
dataset_contributions.detail: Employment-service programmes, provider sites, addresses and contacts.

dataset_contributions.name: QBCC
dataset_contributions.detail: Contractor identity, licence categories, grades and addresses.

dataset_contributions.name: Victorian Liquor
dataset_contributions.detail: Licensees, permits, licensed premises and capacity.

dataset_contributions.name: ASIC Credit
dataset_contributions.detail: Credit-licence status, dates, permissions and conditions.

answer: One extractor read 116/168 columns: 85,446 observations from 7,744 saved rows. Roles separate company facts, contact addresses, sites and licences; unsupported fields remain unmapped. Eight mappings are human-verified, including seven maintainer-corrected configurations: an exception to fully agent-authored mapping.

parts.title: Part 3 — Entity identification
answer: Threshold 0.85 yields 1,455 links across 793 multi-source entities (736 links within the original six sources). Each link retains both source-record IDs, canonical key, confidence and evidence. The 1,245-record unlinked queue explains refusals: weak evidence, ambiguity or conflicting identifiers.

Constrained clusters use ABN, then ACN, then source-record identity as their key anchor; conflicting valid identifiers block merges. Separate licence, site and programme edges preserve one-to-many relationships. Parent/subsidiary ownership is withheld without direct evidence.

Human-confirmed review found 46/50 links correct (92%). This rule-stratified, overlap-enriched sample is not a population estimate. Four failures remain flagged in the proposed output; confidence scores are policy scores, not calibrated probabilities.

parts.title: Part 4 — Company profiles
selection: Fifty profiles combine identity, activities, locations, licences and period-specific finances. Linked-source examples:

profile_examples.name: The Personnel Group Ltd
profile_examples.detail: ACNC size and operating regions plus 11 DEWR establishment records reveal its documented service footprint.

profile_examples.name: WGA Group Holdings Pty Ltd
profile_examples.detail: ASIC identity plus two ATO years show total income rising from AUD 138.65m to 145.31m; these are tax measures, not profit.

profile_examples.name: Chinese Association of Victoria Inc
profile_examples.detail: Charitable purpose combines with a licensed-premises record and BYO permit.

answer: Core/financial claims retain confidence, provenance, alternatives and selection reasons. Reliability-weighted evidence, bounded corroboration and recency determine winners; unsupported facts are absent. Nested site/licence fields retain observation references but still lack complete merged-confidence objects.

Removing ASIC changes 26/50 profiles: 210 field entries disappear, 10 values change and 20 profiles lose multi-source support. Confidence-only changes are excluded. All 25 financially populated profiles depend on ATO; uncorroborated source errors can survive.

part5.title: 1. Cost
answer: One ASIC onboarding run took 15m 25s and used 282,603 input / 30,424 output tokens: US$0.0606 estimated, included above. Subsequent per-record model cost is zero; compute/storage costs were not measured.

part5.title: 2. Agent design
answer: Inspect files, test readers, profile samples, propose mappings, validate held-out rows, critique semantics, revise, then seek human approval. This separates format, execution and interpretation errors. Provider errors retry; exhausted runs checkpoint. Humans see rules, samples, confidence, unmapped fields and validation/critic findings. Semantics is weakest: seven executable mappings needed corrections, including contact addresses treated as sites.

part5.title: 3. The hard one
answer: ASIC supplied a ZIP with tab-separated .csv data and historical-name rows. Reader settings and conditional mappings handle both. Use a custom reader only when the shared configuration cannot represent a format reliably; preserve the canonical output contract.

part5.title: 4. Scale
answer: Acquisition fails first: three of nine initial attempts hit HTTP errors or bot challenges; QBCC's fallback was a biased 32k-row prefix. At 500 sources, add publisher queues, pagination, caching, retry limits and schema/freshness checks. Review needs prioritisation; matching needs persistent candidate indexes and incremental processing.

part5.title: 5. Change
answer: Preserve immutable snapshots/observations, mapping/model/policy versions, candidate evidence, scores, refusals, memberships and human decisions. Run both matchers on identical evidence; compare changed links and cluster splits/merges. Evaluate frozen human labels, review high-impact differences and promote gradually. Rebuild affected profiles, retain old memberships for rollback and publish key aliases/tombstones. Reuse human decisions only while evidence remains applicable.

The implemented comparison retains 1,205 links, adds 250 and removes 363. Evidence-bound review journals exist; automatic corrections, persistent membership history and production rollback remain future work.

part5.title: 6. Next
answer: Week 1: regressions for four failed links and reviewed cluster corrections. Week 2: reliable fetching, schema-drift detection and review/resume controls. Week 3: nested-field confidence, financial-corruption testing and matcher migration with rollback. Correct known errors before scaling.

cost.note: Estimates include logged experiments and retries. Parts 3–4 make no model calls. Chat assistance is excluded; actual billing is unknown.
